answer.rationale: Competitor price cut creates immediate churn pressure on SMB. Memory_73 shows promotional_pricing works for acquisition but materially damages 30-day retention—unsuitable for defense against churn and contradicts primary objective of sustainable revenue. Memory_57 shows referral_incentives work well on established customers with no measurable retention harm, but does not directly address churn risk or price-sensitivity urgency. Memory_86 and memory_91 show onboarding and activation improvements lift engagement, but are slow-acting defenses against immediate churn momentum. Memory_44 establishes that enterprise-assisted sales paths outperform self-serve on pipeline quality and conversion. A standard_experiment shifting sales resources to accelerate enterprise pipeline and revenue diversification avoids the retention cliff of promotional pricing, addresses SMB churn risk indirectly by growing higher-LTV revenue streams, and leverages proven sales-assisted conversion advantage. This preserves long-term unit economics while building revenue resilience. Flagged risk: enterprise sales-assist is not a direct SMB retention tactic and requires sales capacity reallocation; effectiveness depends on execution speed and market appetite. Retains uncertainty about whether enterprise pipeline can absorb resources quickly enough to offset near-term SMB churn.
